Guided reading workshop
fields.summary: What is reading? How is my book made (key vocabulary)? Who made my book (author, illustrator, publisher…)? Why read? Join the guided reading workshop from 4pm.

fields.title: School support for Year 10 pupils with the Université des Montagnes, and board games
fields.summary: See you at the library every Wednesday and Saturday, 10am–3pm. Get school support for Year 10 and give yourself every chance of passing your BEPC. With students from the Université des Montagnes, the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation offers these classes for free. Come and try the new #fibresgacha board games, created with our Paris partner Espace Culturel Gacha.

fields.title: “Tcho la beu”: Medumba tales by Blanche Tchakounté, translated into French
fields.summary: On two Saturdays this month, join Blanche Tchakounté for “Tcho la beu” sessions: tales in Medumba translated into French. Heritage culture comes first! From 10am. Follow our Facebook page to share the experience live: https://www.facebook.com/FondationJFG

fields.title: Fulfulde classes with Aliou
fields.summary: On Saturday 15 May 2021 at 10am, enjoy free Fulfulde classes at the JFG Foundation, open to ages 10 and up, at the JLD Culture Centre. Cultural facilitator Aliou Garga will happily teach you Fulfulde, or Pular, the mother tongue of the Fulani peoples.

fields.title: Poetry and public speaking workshop with slam poet Will’K
fields.summary: Want to try poetry and public speaking? Will’K, the Foundation’s slam poet, welcomes you on Saturday 21 November, ages 14 and up. William Kuihane, known as Will’K, slam artist and cultural facilitator at the Foundation, contributes to children’s arts education in schools.

fields.title: Orphans’ Christmas 2020 – making room for orphans, with the association NA Hope
Medumba literacy classes with Blanche Tchakounté
fields.summary: Literacy classes in Medumba, the most widely spoken language in the Ndé division: come and learn the basics, taught by Blanche, our queen librarian. Passing heritage knowledge on to the next generation.

fields.title: Cultural agenda for May 2021
fields.summary: This May, do what you love – the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation gives you the space to do it. An unprecedented contest for the palm wine makers of Bangoulap. Thank you all for your loyalty, and welcome to newcomers: it’s going to be great. Between Medumba, Fulfulde, talks and sport, happiness…

fields.title: Talk on managing stress before, during and after exams
fields.summary: A talk on managing stress before, during and after exams. When the mind is at ease, the body stays focused… Pupils in exam years are expected on Saturday 24 April at 10am.

fields.title: Community work day on the NGO JFG Foundation site
fields.summary: To celebrate the International Day for Monuments and Sites on 28 May, a community work day will take place on the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation site. Can’t come? Follow our activities online.

fields.title: Music creation workshop
fields.summary: Music creation workshop: the Friends of the Madrigal Choir return to the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation for a workshop based on traditional Bamiléké songs. Choral singing and reflection for young and old.

fields.title: ‘NDOP: cloth of the royal courts and secret societies of Cameroon’, the new book by our president Ly Dumas
fields.summary: Ndop – you are at once ceremonial cloth, weaving tradition, a mythology of signs and a source of inspiration for today’s designers. Worn by the kings, queens and dignitaries of the chiefdoms of West Cameroon, you link the living and the dead, the invisible, the earth and the cosmos. ‘NDOP: cloth of the royal courts and secret societies of Cameroon’ by Ly Dumas is available at the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation, the Zingana hotel, FNAC Douala, and soon in museums in Cameroon and abroad. Each purchase helps fund our cultural and community work.

fields.title: Celebrating International Museum Day
fields.summary: Celebrating International Museum Day: as an open-air museum, the NGO Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation takes part with a discussion on the genealogy and history of the people of the Ndé.

fields.title: Debrief of the 2021 General Assembly seminar of the NGO Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation
fields.summary: The Foundation’s staff look back at how they work as a team. This year’s General Assembly took the unusual form of a seminar at the end of February, bringing together members of Espace Culturel Gacha in Paris and of the Foundation in Cameroon to review the year’s achievements and prepare the months ahead, inspired by the Foundation’s origins.

fields.title: Vacances Utiles 2021 is under way
fields.summary: This year’s Vacances Utiles invites you to discover: visual arts, beadwork, design, dance, African art, music and singing, comics, theatre, public speaking and slam, writing and reading, Medumba and Fulfulde, French and English classes, dictation and mental arithmetic, and a discovery trip to Bandjoun Station and Batoufam.

fields.title: Blogging workshops on using the internet and social media well
fields.summary: During the summer programme, young people from Bangoulap and nearby will take part in a workshop on blogging in the digital age. Educating young people about social media, and peace through social media, will be the main topics. See you on 10 and 11 August, 10am–2pm, in the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation auditorium. All the photos are on the Foundation’s Facebook page: https://www.facebook.com/FondationJFG

fields.title: The Boutang’ART exhibition continues at the Gacha Foundation
fields.summary: Discover the exhibition by painter Guillaume Yanga at the Foundation’s shop, featuring heritage motifs from the land of Bangoulap.

fields.title: The wonders of the beadwork workshop at Artcurial, Paris
fields.summary: Four wicker baskets, embroidered and beaded by the women of the Gacha Foundation’s beadwork workshop in Cameroon, are on show this weekend for the Africa2020 Season and the exhibition “Exceptions d’Afrique”, a selection of gems of contemporary African art. At Artcurial, 7 rond-point des Champs-Élysées, 75008 Paris, 12–14 June 2021.

fields.title: Vacances Utiles continues with the Friends of the Madrigal Choir of Cameroon
fields.summary: This week’s singing lessons will be performed by the children on Friday 20 August at the closing of the summer programme. Yes, we are nearing the end of eight intense weeks of games and activities for children from the Foundation and beyond. Book your place now for next year’s 7th edition, which will celebrate our wonderful Foundation’s 20th anniversary. More photos and videos on our Facebook page.

fields.title: Cultural agenda for October 2021
fields.summary: This October, the Gacha Foundation offers a varied programme of indoor and outdoor activities: storytelling, films for young people, do-it-yourself workshops and, for the adventurous, a hike to the Nyagma hyena cave. This month also sees the launch of a reading and writing project for young people: come and discover the writer in you!

fields.title: The Gacha Foundation at the Hilton hotel craft fair in Yaoundé
fields.summary: On Saturday 2 October 2021, the Hilton hotel in Yaoundé held a craft fair showcasing Cameroonian products.

fields.title: Best palm wine maker contest at the Matango club, Villa Boutanga
fields.summary: The palm wine makers of Bangoulap show their skills at the Matango club, Villa Boutanga. Each candidate is judged on three points: introducing themselves, their family and their genealogy in the local language and in French (5 points) – testing their eloquence and knowledge of their lineage; their knowledge of the uses and heritage of palm wine (10 points) – what is palm wine, which traditional events in Bamiléké country, and in Bangoulap in particular, involve it, and what are its virtues; and finally the quality of their wine (5 points).

fields.title: Hike: discovering Cameroon’s natural heritage
fields.summary: A hike through Cameroon’s natural heritage. In this green, mountainous landscape, the Gacha Foundation takes you on a journey to meet raffia wine makers and discover this local craft.

fields.title: Screening of “The Jungle Book” and a tale in Fulfulde
fields.summary: Relive this friendly moment with the children on Saturday 30 October, with tales and a film screening.

fields.title: Medumba tales and film screening on 16 October
fields.summary: On Saturday 16 October 2021, join us for a children’s tale in Medumba and a screening of the film “The Girl with the Blue Eyes”.

fields.title: Cultural agenda for November 2021
fields.summary: November promises to be full of varied activities. The NGO Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation looks forward to seeing you there! Discover the programme.

fields.title: Craft and social workshop for women at the Foundation
fields.summary: At the start of October, the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation offered women a three-day course on making natural detergents and soaps. The workshop is part of a social approach to tackling poverty and idleness.

fields.title: Educational talk with young people: the dangers of drug use
fields.summary: Join us at the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation for talks on rarely discussed topics, to think together and speak freely.

fields.title: Cultural agenda for December 2021
fields.summary: Tales by the fire, traditional dances, the unbeatable grilled plantain with red palm oil, and plenty of activities specially prepared for New Year’s Eve in Boutanga village. On top of this tempting programme, the children will go on a dream trip to Mount Mbapit – and many more surprises await in the last month of the year.

fields.title: Cultural agenda for January 2022
fields.summary: Happy New Year and good health from all the teams in Bangoulap! We are delighted to see you again this year for an even richer programme. Caroline Viallatte returns to the Foundation to run workshops on breast milk with hospital staff from the region.

fields.title: Medumba tales on Saturday 3 November 2021
fields.summary: Children are invited to listen to tales in Medumba, translated into French by Blanche Tchakounté and Théophile Nkaba – a learning moment to discover and get to know the language that is part of their culture.

fields.title: Class outing: screening of Black Panther
fields.summary: A trip to Wakanda with the Black Panther team for a class outing: culture and heritage in an extraordinary universe.

fields.title: The holidays were a resounding success!
fields.summary: A big thank you to all the volunteers and artists who contributed to this 7th edition, to our Paris branch Espace Culturel Gacha for its constant support, especially in fundraising, to our sponsors, to the Foundation’s teams and, of course, to our young holidaymakers who took part in every activity with great enthusiasm. See you next year for the 8th edition. Have a great start to the school year!

fields.title: February 2023 programme
fields.summary: General Assembly month, access to health month, youth awareness month: the Foundation is very active once again.

fields.title: Vacances Utiles 2022 #SaveTheDate
fields.summary: A rich and colourful 7th edition of Vacances Utiles, with even more children, discoveries and workshops in Medumba, Fulfulde, French and English, visual arts, poetry, and new volunteers sharing their talents. Just save the date!

fields.title: Discovery trip to Mount Mbapit
fields.summary: December brought joy to the children with a discovery trip to the crater lake of Mount Mbapit, between Foumbot and Foumban. With the association NA Hope, children from the JLD Culture Centre and from the Bonne Case orphanage in Bangangté shared this wonderful experience with our guides Aliou, William and Christelle, among others.

fields.title: Creative residency – interview with Alice Ifergan Rey
fields.summary: Alice Ifergan Rey is a performance artist who for several years has been creating masks for horses and riders, to build an aesthetic and relational continuity between them. Alice chose the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation for her creative residency. She arrived on the red earth of Bangoulap on 16 March 2023 to make a partly beaded horse mask using the traditional beadwork technique of the Foundation’s craftswomen. Read about her artistic approach.

fields.title: The Foundation takes part in International Museum Day organised by ICOM
fields.summary: International Museum Day 2023, organised by ICOM (International Council of Museums) on the theme of the environment and well-being, will be celebrated at the Foundation with activities showcasing local crafts and raising visitors’ awareness of protecting our environment. Discover the programme.

fields.title: Collaboration: Lutz Morris × Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation
fields.summary: Discover the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation’s latest collaboration with the handbag brand Lutz Morris: made between Germany and Cameroon, celebrating craftsmanship, responsible production, exchange and generosity.

fields.title: Dexeus × Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation project
fields.summary: Committed to the health of communities, the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation coordinates care, medical interventions and infrastructure support.

fields.title: International Museum Week at the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation
fields.summary: International Museum Day 2023, organised by ICOM on the theme of the environment and the well-being of communities, was celebrated at the Foundation with activities that showcased local crafts and raised visitors’ awareness of protecting our environment.

fields.title: June programme at the Foundation
Bringing water through technological innovation
fields.summary: The Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation announces a new, visionary project to meet communities’ water needs by installing machines that turn air into drinking water.

fields.title: Supporting research
fields.summary: Espace Culturel Gacha and the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation supported academic research: Clarisse Darnaude, a master’s student at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University, was welcomed by both institutions to gather information for her thesis on promoting Ndop cloth.

fields.title: Bringing education – building the Maroua school
fields.summary: With the support of Espace Culturel Gacha, the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation will build a nursery school in Dogba, Maroua II district, in North Cameroon.

fields.title: Vacances Utiles 2023 – 8th edition
fields.summary: The 8th Vacances Utiles runs from 3 July to 25 August at the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation. The programme gives around a hundred young people educational activities over the summer: workshops in Medumba, Fulfulde, French and English; culture, poetry and visual arts; games and sport…

fields.title: The right to education – a donation of school supplies
fields.summary: As part of the cooperation between the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation and Espace Culturel Gacha, the Jean-Félicien Gacha school in Manoré, founded in 2014, received a donation of school supplies to secure and strengthen the right to education.

fields.title: Children’s literature – Yaya and Tita’s Ndop
fields.summary: Following the academic book “Ndop, cloth of the royal courts”, the result of years of work by authors, collectors and anthropologists, discover the enchanting world of “Yaya and Tita’s Ndop”: a captivating journey into the tradition of the royal Ndop cloth, written for younger generations.

fields.title: The Dexeus Mujer Foundation 2023 Prize awarded to Ly Dumas
fields.summary: The Spanish Dexeus Mujer Foundation has awarded its prize to Ly Dumas, president and founder of the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation.

fields.title: Philosophy workshops for young people
fields.summary: Philosophy workshops on the idea of happiness were offered to several of the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation’s partner schools.

fields.title: Teaching excellence in hospitality and catering
fields.summary: The “Académie Hôtelière des Grasslands” hotel school will soon open on Boutanga hill in Bangoulap, in the Bangangté district. It will offer young people from Cameroon and the Central African region excellent training in hospitality, catering and tourism.

fields.title: The Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation becomes a member of ICOM!
fields.summary: The Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation joins ICOM, the International Council of Museums.

fields.title: Looking back on 2022
fields.summary: From the Bourgogne Tribal Show and the Révélations fair to the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation’s 20th anniversary: our 2022 highlights!

fields.title: Shared synergies: Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation / International Museum Day / ICOM
fields.summary: For International Museum Day 2024, organised by ICOM, the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation held a round table on museums for education and research on Saturday 18 May.

fields.title: Safeguarding intangible heritage – collecting Cameroon’s traditional songs
fields.summary: We are delighted to renew our partnership with the Friends of the Madrigal Choir of Cameroon! It continues the first song collection held in Bangoulap in 2021. This year, the project travels in July to the East, North and North-West regions of Cameroon.

fields.title: Maison Gacha is born!
fields.summary: Ly Dumas, founder and president of the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation, Frédéric Dumas and Édouard Dumas, president of Espace Culturel Gacha, are delighted to announce the creation of Maison Gacha.

fields.title: Opening of the exhibition “Between Spirit and Earth: traditional African textile art” at the Pinacoteca de São Paulo, Brazil
fields.summary: The Pinacoteca de São Paulo and Paris-based Maison Gacha present the exhibition “Between Spirit and Earth: traditional African textile art”, in collaboration with the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation in Bangoulap, Cameroon.

fields.title: Ly Dumas made a Knight of the Cameroonian National Order of Merit
fields.summary: On 5 June, Ly Dumas, founder and president of the NGO Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation, was awarded the medal of Knight of the Cameroonian National Order of Merit.

fields.title: Bangoulap au cœur du livre: first edition at the Jean-Félicien Gacha Foundation
fields.summary: A unique event for culture and knowledge! In a spirit of sharing and exchange, authors, artists and book lovers gather from 13 to 20 January 2025 to celebrate the richness of African literature. Creative workshops, literary residencies, book signings, a pop-up bookshop, literary safaris, cultural discoveries and much more will fill this week of celebration. Bangoulap au cœur du livre!

fields.title: Creative residency – Barbara Asei Dantoni
fields.summary: Barbara Asei Dantoni is a French-Italian-Cameroonian artist and designer whose studio is based between France and Cameroon.

fields.title: In pictures: the opening of the exhibition “Between Spirit and Earth: traditional African textile art”
fields.summary: Open to the public since 31 August, the exhibition presents a major body of African textile art to a Latin American audience for the first time.

fields.title: Children’s literature: publication of “Adi de Boutanga”
